subject: Pilot extension: convert unused days to engineering-hours credit or short bridge
messages:
From: Darci Liu <darci@nimblewave.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — 2-week runway + convert unused days into engineering support?

Hi Vivek,

Hope you had a good weekend. We hit a small blocker on our data ingestion path and will need ~2 extra weeks to complete the validation for the pilot. Our legal/procurement team is generally OK with short extensions, but they'd prefer to exchange value instead of a straight time-only extension.

Question: is Redwood open to converting the remainder of our unused pilot days into a block of engineering-hours we can book with your solutions team (e.g., integration support / model tuning)? If so, what would that conversion look like (hours, rate, expiration)? Alternatively, if that's not possible, could we get a short 2-week runway with a small top-up of credits?

We'd like to get alignment this week so procurement can sign the amendment and we avoid losing momentum. CC'ing our point person, procurement@nimblewave.com for visibility.

Thanks,
Darci
Darci Liu
Head of ML Platform
NimbleWave

[Attachment: sprint-log-issue-231.txt (text, 3KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Darci Liu <darci@nimblewave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week runway + convert unused days into engineering support?

Hi Darci — thanks for the note and the context. Totally understand the need to keep the pilot moving. We can do this two ways depending on what procurement prefers:

Option A — Time extension + token cap hold
- 2-week extension (no additional fee)
- Token cap reduced by 15% during the extra window (keeps unit economics intact)
- Standard pilot terms remain in force

Option B — Convert unused pilot days into engineering-hours credit
- Convert remaining pilot days into a block of engineering-hours (bookable with our Solutions Eng team)
- We propose 20 engineering hours per 10 unused pilot days, expiring 90 days after execution
- Rate equivalent: list engineering rate $250/hr, we can offer the conversion at an internal billing rate equal to a 35% discount off list (so effectively $162.50/hr for accounting)

I've drafted a short amendment that outlines both options and the mechanics — attaching for your review. If procurement likes the engineering-hours route we can wire a DocuSign link for signature and route the SOW/booking flow.

Next steps: tell us which option (A or B) you prefer and whether procurement needs us to show the cost as an invoice adjustment or as a credited-hours line.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: amendment_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 34KB)]

From: Darci Liu <darci@nimblewave.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimblewave.com
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week runway + convert unused days into engineering support?

Vivek,

Thanks — option B sounds closer to what our team needs, but a couple of procurement/ops clarifications before we can sign:
1) Can the engineering-hours be used for integration work (data connectors, deployment checks) and also limited tuning sessions? Our PMs want flexibility.
2) Is the 90-day expiry soft (can it be extended once with mutual agreement) or firm?
3) Procurement would like to see the conversion expressed as a credit line on the amendment (they don't want a separate invoice).
4) Finally, is there any concurrency cap on what we can book (we might need a few half-days concurrently during a sprint).

If you can confirm these points we can get procurement to review the amendment this week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Darci

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Darci Liu <darci@nimblewave.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, procurement@nimblewave.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 2-week runway + convert unused days into engineering support?

Hey Darci — Marissa here (AE on the account). Quick answers to help procurement move: 

1) Use cases: Yes — hours can be booked for integration support, connector work, incident triage, or targeted model-tuning sessions. We'll include a short booking policy in the amendment that lists accepted activities.
2) Expiry: 90 days is standard; we can add a one-time, mutual-agreement extension of up to 30 days (must be agreed in writing before expiry).
3) Accounting format: We'll show the conversion as a credited-hours line on the amendment (no separate invoice). That meets procurement's ask.
4) Concurrency: No hard concurrency cap, but we request that bookings over 4 hours/day be scheduled at least 5 business days in advance so we can coordinate SE availability. Ad-hoc half-day slots are fine.

I've also attached a short pilot-terms-summary spreadsheet that maps unused days -> hours under the conversion formula so procurement can see the math.

If that sounds good, I'll update the amendment to show the credited-hours line and include the DocuSign flow. Can you confirm a PO number or procurement contact for routing?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pilot-terms-summary.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]

Marissa / Vivek — this all looks fine. Procurement approves option B as a credited-hours line; PO will be issued once DocuSign is returned. Our procurement contact is procurement@nimblewave.com (CC'd).

Please proceed with the amendment showing: 20 eng-hours per 10 unused days; $162.50/hr effective conversion rate; 90-day expiry with one 30-day mutual extension; credit line on the amendment. SE booking policy as outlined is acceptable.

I'll expect the DocuSign link and will route to our finance team today. Thanks for the quick support — this will keep our pilot on schedule.

—Darci
